goal: Build Gleam, a Chrome MV3 Arweave/AO browser-extension wallet: password-protected vault, AR/AO balances and transfers, activity feed, tagged uploads, and an ArConnect-compatible injected provider with connection and signing approval flows.
outcome: A user can install the extension, create or import a wallet, unlock it, see AR and AO token balances, send and receive AR, view a merged activity feed, upload tagged content to Arweave, and connect/sign through the injected provider from a dApp — with every signing action reviewed in its own approval window showing a decoded preview and a verifiable payload hash.

requirements.statement: core package logic (vault, keys, signing, arweave/ao clients, pricing, activity, policy, models) has zero chrome.*/window/document dependency, enforced via an ESLint no-restricted-imports rule.
Plaintext key-material buffers are zeroized (.fill(0)) in a finally block after both encrypt and decrypt, including error paths.
Storage is treated as untrusted input: every record read back is re-validated (ports range-checked, permissions filtered against an allowlist, malformed records dropped) on every load.
A page-originated message can only ever reach PROVIDER_METHODS, never KEY_METHODS or APPROVAL_METHODS — enforced at a single dispatcher choke point.
AR balances and amounts are handled as Winston atomic-integer strings throughout, never converted to a floating-point number at any layer.
Full, untruncated addresses are shown on every send-review, receive, and signing-approval screen; truncation is only acceptable in low-stakes list views (activity list).
Both light and dark themes ship together from the first screen, defined as CSS custom properties, never color-defined only inside a media query.
Container queries (not viewport breakpoints) drive responsive layout across popup/sidepanel/approval surfaces.

Branding, visual design, UX copy, and screen layout follow the existing material in the sibling ao-wallet repo (brand/guidelines.md, brand/voice.md, and the 16 built HTML mockups under screens/) directly — not redesigned from scratch.
Vault password must be >=10 characters and rejected if it matches a common/breached-password blocklist check.
A generated JWK is encrypted into the vault envelope before touching any storage; plaintext key material is never persisted.
An invalid/malformed imported keyfile is rejected with a specific reason, not a generic error.
Keyfile backup/download is offered at creation time, explicit and skippable, never forced or hidden.
Unlock tries the last-active wallet's password, then opportunistically the same password against other stored wallets, failing silently per-wallet on mismatch.
Default auto-lock timeout is never; manual Lock now always available and immediately clears unlocked-session state.
The unlock screen shows no per-wallet identity (avatar/name/address).
Forgot password leads to an explicit, plainly-worded destructive reset (wipes all locally stored vaults), never a silent delete.
Unlocked-session metadata lives in memory-only storage (chrome.storage.session), never written to disk.
AR balance is read via GET {gateway}/wallet/{address}/balance and rendered without float conversion.
AO token balance is read via the HyperBEAM process@1.0 compute path for a given processId/address.
Send review screen shows the full recipient address, amount, fee, and total; a first-seen-address escalates to Irreversible-tier framing.
Send submission writes an optimistic activity entry immediately, before gateway confirmation.
Receive screen shows the full address with a QR code and a one-tap copy affordance.
Activity feed is the union of the local action log and one gateway GraphQL transactions query by owner and recipient, most-recent-N.
Transaction detail view shows the full untruncated tx id and tags.
Upload tag byte size is capped at ~4096 bytes, enforced live during composition.
A pre-upload secret scan rejects/flags payloads resembling a private key/JWK/PEM block before submission, stating the specific match type.
The injected provider is added via a removable <script src> tag at document_start, top frame only, and never clobbers an existing window.arweaveWallet.
connect() requests show the origin and requested permission scopes before creating a grant; approval opens in its own window, never inline in the popup.
Signing approval shows recipient, amount, fee, a decoded-data preview, tags, and a SHA-256 hash of the exact signing payload with its own copy affordance, before approval is possible.
If no wallet exists when a signing request arrives, the approval window switches to onboarding in place and returns to the pending request afterward.
Revoking a grant ends all access it covered; a revoked origin must be re-approved via a fresh connect() before any further provider call succeeds.
Network/peer settings allow adding/removing AO-Core/HyperBEAM peer URLs with a per-peer enable toggle that switches the active endpoint(s).
Removing a wallet with no confirmed backup warns explicitly that access will be lost permanently before proceeding.
